A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Factuality Matters work. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on StructBench and ImgEdit-Full, explicit-reasoning experiments, and a human-preference alignment study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Nano Banana 2.0 benchmark scores and qualitative editing and generalization examples.

M1.justification: The FLUX.1 Kontext/Qwen-VL architecture, MLP connector, mask-based loss weighting, three-stage training, and external reasoning procedure are unchanged. Atomic Q&A refinement was already described in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 and Figure 16 add qualitative testing on Nano Banana 2-generated scenes containing structured visuals in realistic surroundings. Existing training datasets, StructBench, and ImgEdit-Full remain. The corrected six-domain enumeration does not add Science coverage; v1 already evaluated it.

E2.justification: Nano Banana 2.0 is added alongside the original Nano Banana in Tables 1–3. Comparator membership in the Qwen-evaluator comparisons, reasoning experiment, and ImgEdit-Full comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: Retained experiments use the same benchmark counts, evaluators, StructScore weighting, resolution handling, and training settings. The new qualitative cases extend input coverage without a separately specified change to scoring, splits, budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 supplies six ImgEdit-Full editing examples, and Figure 16 supplies four cases probing transfer to realistic synthetic scenes. The atomic-Q&A reliability analysis, explicit-reasoning study, human alignment analysis, and weighting ablation already appear in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 50 shuffled-order Elo computations and reporting means and standard deviations, with unchanged Elo parameters. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: The added baseline substantially changes the main-table rankings: Nano Banana 2.0 scores 67.05 on editing versus v1's leading 55.98, and 92.00 on T2I versus 49.58. Its chart-editing score is 63.28 versus the previous leader's 50.58. Existing scores remain unchanged; Figures 10 and 16 add qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: The Elo definitions and equations (1)–(3) are retained, moving from Appendix A.3 to A.4. No mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the dataset, model, benchmark, and reasoning contributions. The introduction's best-editing claim also remains unchanged despite the higher-scoring new comparator.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly interprets Figure 16 as evidence of generalization beyond code-rendered structured images and of the dataset's usefulness. Existing interpretations and future-work boundaries remain; the main discussion is not reconciled with the new baseline results.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Nano Banana 2 as the generator of the new generalization inputs and provides editing instructions with the added qualitative examples. Existing training hyperparameters, construction/evaluation prompt templates, hardware statements, and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior work are unchanged. Most related work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A.1, while the benchmark discussion moves into the introduction.

P1.justification: v2 relocates related work, adds acknowledgments, corrects the domain enumeration, and updates section references and publication headers. Most explanatory prose remains unchanged, so the restructuring is limited.

P2.justification: v2 adds qualitative Figures 10 and 16 and expands Tables 1–3 with a comparator row. The atomic-Q&A illustration moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure 15, and existing panels are rearranged. The other visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The updated baseline comparison and qualitative transfer examples add useful evidence. However, Section 5.2 still calls 55.98 the highest editing score and 49.58 the best T2I score, and says the best models achieve about half accuracy, despite Tables 1–2 reporting 67.05 and 92.00. The empirical additions and newly conflicting conclusions leave the net quality change uncertain.
